## Core

### Bugfixes
- Failed TUI worker requests now return an error instead of leaving the caller hanging. (@Nowaker)

**Thank you to 1 community contributor:**
- @Nowaker:
  - fix(opencode): answer a failed TUI worker request instead of hanging (#54936)

### New Features

- **Fork sessions whose folder is gone**: when a session's original folder was moved or deleted, you can now fork it into the current folder instead of only continuing, so later resumes no longer ask. See [Continue or switch sessions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.2/packages/coding-agent/docs/sessions.md#continue-or-switch-sessions).

### Changed

- When a session's working directory no longer exists, for example after the project folder was renamed, interactive mode now offers `Continue`, `Fork`, or `Cancel` instead of only continuing. `Continue` runs the session in the current directory without storing the choice, as before; `Fork` copies it into the current directory as a new session with a new ID, like `--fork`, so the next resume no longer asks. This applies at startup (`--session`, `--resume`), to `/resume`, to `/import`, and to `ctx.switchSession()` from extensions ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))

### Fixed

- Fixed `/import` of a session whose working directory no longer exists leaving a copy in the session directory, and continuing it leaving a second copy with the same ID (`s.jsonl` and `s-1.jsonl`); the failed copy is now removed ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))
- Fixed Anthropic OAuth requests reporting an outdated Claude Code version

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **Native Approvals for Harness Agents**: Claude's and Codex's own permission requests now reach the AgentOS approval UI. When the agent has a database, including one AgentOS supplies, a native request persists a PAUSED run that shows up in the existing chat and Approvals views, and Resolve plus Continue Run delivers the decision back to the same native execution without replaying the prompt. The harness's own policy decides when to ask — Claude keeps its `permission_mode` and explicit permission callbacks, Codex supports `approval_policy="on-request" | "untrusted" | "never"` alongside its existing SDK `auto_review` and `deny_all` modes — so there is no separate Agno setting to turn on. Decisions are validated against the exact action requested, with sync and async continuation, cancellation, expiry and storage-failure handling, and sandboxed agents keep this across Docker and AgentCore: capability negotiation, a decision RPC, fenced persistence, reattachment after an API-worker loss, separate approval-wait and execution budgets, and no replay after process loss. Note that a `CodexAgent` with no approval settings now runs under the native `on-request` policy, so a request that previously went nowhere pauses the run instead; `hitl_timeout` (default 900s) bounds how long it waits. See `cookbook/frameworks/human_in_the_loop/`.

# Skill toggles, tool timers and a faster Hyper ⚡ This release was brought to you by our team and our favorite contributors! Long awaited features ahead, read along! ## Toggle skills Skills can now be switched on and off right from the command palette. Broken skills are easy to spot, too! (they're marked with a red × and the reason they failed) ## 🕐 How long is this taking? Every tool call now shows how long it's been running. Now, you'll know whether that test suite is just slow or actually stuck. ## Lighter, faster Hyper ⚡ Requests to Hyper are now compressed with [Brotli](https://brotli.org/) 🥦. That means much smaller uploads on every turn and snappier responses, especially in long sessions. Hyper now also supports [Gzip](https://www.gzip.org/) that other agents could use when Brotli if not viable. Big thanks to @BrunoKrugel for the first 2 awesome features! See more below ⬇️ Have a great Thursday, Charm XX 🌞 ## Changelog ### New! * 2b7816fed084f029f4061e441a6f9f3980e71c21: feat(skill): toggle skills (#3994) (@BrunoKrugel) * 7f9e4824c465e1ffa1a1d652dd6e9a897b54035c: feat(ui): Add elapsed time on tool call (#3600) (@BrunoKrugel) * f38c0dc030912cc3eeaa82cfb014cf21868405b0: feat: add CRUSH_DATA_DIR env var to override the project data

### Added

- Installed plugins can be turned off with the `disabled_plugins` setting: a disabled plugin stays installed but contributes nothing to sessions
- Plugins can be off by default (`defaultEnabled: false` in their `ai.mistral.vibe` extension) and turned on with the `enabled_plugins` setting
- `/skills` lists your installed skills, one row per name, with search, a Space toggle to turn each one on or off, and the highlighted skill's body under the list or beside it on wide terminals.
- With registry skills on, `/skills` lists shared skills to add on a Shared tab and lets you pin a version or alias per scope, preview each version, unpin a scope, or remove the skill.

### Changed

- With registry skills on, a project's skills, files or pins, win over global ones of the same name, including skills from `skill_paths`.
- With registry skills on, cached shared skill versions unused for 30 days are deleted when the registry can still serve them.
- While the agent only waits for background work, the status line says what it waits for and that a message reaches it at once.
- A tool group header now counts the calls still running apart from the settled ones ("Calling 1 tool, called 2 tools").
- Opening a session no longer fetches the model catalog: it is cached on disk and refreshed in the background, and running sessions pick up the refresh when their turn ends
- Crash reports now cover app-server and session resume errors, and no longer include routine error logs or network outages.

### Fixed

- Headless --max-tokens and --max-price limits now stop the run before another roo

## 🖇️  Connect your Claude Pro or Max subscription

If you have a Claude Pro or Max subscription, Plandex can use it when calling Anthropic models. You can use it in either Integrated Models Mode on Plandex Cloud, or in BYO Key Mode (whether on Cloud or self-hosting).

Assuming you're using Anthropic models (which the default model pack does), you'll be asked if you want to connect your Claude subscription the first time you run Plandex. Follow the instructions to connect.

[Learn more in the docs.](https://docs.plandex.ai/models/claude-subscription)

# Nanobrowser v0.3.0

Nanobrowser 0.3 is rebuilt from the ground up: one agent in the side panel, on top of a new browser control layer that clicks the right element, acts like a real user and reports what really happened.

## What's new

- **CDP.** The new browser control is rebuilt with chrome.debugger API, it uses CDP to interact with elements in web pages. It's more stable than the previous injected scripts solution.
- **One agent, one chat per tab.** The old planner and navigator are replaced by a single agent. Several tasks can run side by side, each in its own tab group.
- **You decide what it may do.** Ask mode (default) asks before the agent submits, sends, deletes or uploads; Auto mode goes ahead. Payments, passwords, codes and access grants are always handed to you. Set any site to Allow, Ask or Block.
- **More reliable actions.** Each element has an ID tied to that exact element, clicks and typing are real browser input, and every action is sent once and reports whether the page responded.
- **Any model with tool calling.** Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Grok, DeepSeek, Mistral, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama and LM Studio. Pick the model and reasoning effort per chat; Test models in Settings checks which ones work.
- **Attachments and uploads.** Attach images, text files or a screenshot of the tab; the agent can upload your files to a page and save results (CSV, Markdown) to Downloads.
- **Shortcuts, voice and custom instructions.** Start saved prompts with `/`, speak with OpenAI's or Gemini's voice model, and tell the agent what to

## Highlights

### Knowledge v2: page-tree model, richer tools, and server-side sync APIs
Knowledge is now a first-class page tree (pages/notes/pins) with major tool upgrades: `knowledge_list`, line/section/grep-style reads in `knowledge_read`, list pinning (`kind: 'list'`), and a link index for counting/listing `[[links]]`. Apps can also sync external content via server APIs like `knowledge.upsertPage()`/`removePage()` and note upserts, with optional vector/hybrid search and chunked embeddings for very long pages.

### Knowledge Explorer + read-only Knowledge HTTP/JS client APIs (and SSE change stream)
Mastra Server now offers opt-in read-only Knowledge routes (tree/page/graph/search/activity) plus an SSE events stream, with matching `listKnowledge()` / `getKnowledge()` APIs in `@mastra/client-js`. These routes are scope-gated (and FGA-aware) and enable building Knowledge browsing UIs outside Studio, including link-count/link-edge endpoints when the store supports the link index.

### Durable agent continuity across API restarts (fencing + shared storage requirement)
Evented durable agents no longer stop when the API process shuts down: workers continue running, clean up, and free threads correctly, with improved run ownership isolation and safer cancellation semantics. To get true cross-process continuity you now need fencing-capable shared storage (e.g. `PostgresStore` from `@mastra/pg`) plus shared pubsub/lease infrastructure.

### Background tasks + MCP: resumable “input required” flows that survive reloads
Suspended background tool calls can now be resumed

## ⭐️ Highlights

### 🧭 Classify and Route with the OpenAI Decisions API
Three new components use the OpenAI Decisions API to choose how to handle your data without instructions. [`OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionstextrouter) sends text to a named output per label, [`OpenAIDecisionsImageRouter`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionsimagerouter) does the same for images and can send low-confidence decisions to a fallback branch, and [`OpenAIDecisionsDocumentClassifier`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionsdocumentclassifier) answers choice, score, and yes/no questions about documents and stores the answers in their metadata.

```python
from haystack.components.routers import OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter

router = OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter(
    labels={
        "billing": "Payments, invoices, refunds and charges",
        "technical": "Bugs, crashes and errors in the product",
    },
    instructions="Which team should handle this support request?",
    min_confidence=0.6,
)

print(router.run(text="I was charged twice for my subscription."))
# >> {'billing': 'I was charged twice for my subscription.'}
```

### 🧱 Structured Output for Agents
The new [`StructuredOutputHook`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/structured-output) validates the Agent's final reply against a Pydantic model or JSON schema and returns it as a dict in `result["structured_output"]`. If the reply doesn't validate, the hook sends the error back to the model and lets it try again, up to `max_retries` times.

## Features

- Tracing now runs on `opentelemetry-api` alone and emits OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention spans, so any OTLP backend reads them: a plain collector, Grafana Tempo, Sentry, Datadog, Honeycomb, PostHog, Jaeger, Arize Phoenix, Langfuse. Phoenix and the OpenInference packages are no longer required.
- One `chat {model}` CLIENT span per Instructor attempt, driven by Instructor hooks: per-attempt and total usage (input, output, cached and reasoning tokens) for both chat-completion and Responses shapes, `gen_ai.response.model`, attempt count, validation errors as events, `error.type` on failures. Totals also land on the agent span.
- `AgentConfig(name=...)` gives agents a stable span name (`invoke_agent {name}`); `using_conversation(conversation_id)` sets `gen_ai.conversation.id` on everything inside the block.
- `TracingConfig(hide_inputs, hide_outputs, max_attribute_length, openinference_attributes, llm_spans)` replaces ad-hoc keyword options, with environment equivalents `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_HIDE_INPUTS`, `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_HIDE_OUTPUTS`, `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_MAX_ATTRIBUTE_LENGTH` and `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_LLM_SPANS`. The `OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_*` variables still work as a fallback.
- Hiding is applied before serialization and wins over truncation. Under `hide_outputs` every exception is reduced to `<Type>: <N> attempts (__REDACTED__)` and traceback frames carry no source lines, so retry exhaustion cannot leak model output.
- Cancellation (`CancelledError`, `GeneratorExit`) is recorded as `atomic_agents.cancelled=true` with status UNSET on agent and tool spans

# Agent Zero — Release Notes

## Highlights

This is a large release that promotes core tools into standalone plugins, overhauls the welcome screen, hardens channel security, improves streaming and UI responsiveness, and adds new search, migration, and documentation capabilities.

---

## Tool Plugin Architecture

- **Extracted bundled tools into standalone plugins:** `wait`, `notify_user`, `search_engine`, `a2a_chat`, `scheduler`, `behavior_adjustment`, and the scheduler Tasks UI are now standard plugins, each with dedicated badge styling, log types, and prompt files.
- **Unified memory tools:** The four separate `memory_load`, `memory_save`, `memory_delete`, and `memory_forget` tools are consolidated into a single `memory` tool with an `action` argument, matching the action-dispatch pattern used by other tools.
- **Per-action tool permissions:** Profiles can now allow or deny individual operations across all 12 bundled multi-action tools (e.g., allow file reads but block writes, or allow listing scheduled tasks but block deletion). The Agent Editor shows grouped action controls with expandable entries.
- **Centralized boolean argument coercion** across all promoted and core tools, removing duplicated helpers and strict-validation error paths.
- **Dedicated badge rendering** for goal, document_query, skills, vision, browser, office, and computer_use_remote tool calls, each with distinct accent colors and descriptive headlines.
- **Dropped agent-name prefix** from all tool log headlines, warning rows, and fallback entries for cleaner chat output.
